principles.text: Give agents tasks, not problems: clear, well-specified, easy-to-verify work beats open-ended asks.
The right product form factor is a function of model capability, so revisit it every two to three months.
Price AI around 10x cheaper than the human time it replaces, and judge it by outcomes, not tokens.
Startups beat giants by narrowing focus on one concentrated bet and caring more about it than they do.
Think stickiness, not moats: build learning and multiplayer use that compound the longer a team uses it.

sampleQA.question: How should I price an AI agent product?

answer.text: Move from per-seat to usage-based pricing: the AI agents are effectively seats, and costs track GPU spend.
Aim to be roughly 10x cheaper than the value of the human time the agent replaces.
Measure value in productive engineering hours, not tokens or lines of code. Cognition backs this with a guarantee of up to $10M in credits.

sampleQA.question: What should my first enterprise use case be?

answer.text: Pick repetitive, tightly scoped tasks with a fast feedback loop, like code migrations: not the hardest work, and not so simple a script could do it.
Look for use cases with 10x gains, not 10-20% ROI.
For the first customer, do things that don't scale. Cognition deployed the whole company onsite in Brazil.

sampleQA.question: How do you compete with the foundation model labs?

answer.text: Stay model-neutral and build a compound system that routes each subtask to the best model; customers trust a neutral partner.
Solve the messy real-world context labs skip: the data, the tools, and defining the benchmark for success.
As a startup, your edge has to be speed and focus.
